fields.meaning: Based on…, on the basis of…
examples: We developed products based on the survey results.
This book was written by the professor based on many years of research.
Classes will be decided based on the test results.
Based on the plan, construction will begin next month.
The policy is being reviewed based on the latest statistics.
The company took disciplinary action based on its internal regulations.
fields.explain:
Formal nuance; often found in administrative documents, laws, reports, and guidelines.
Nouns before「に基づいて」are usually:法律,規則,方針,計画, データ,統計,事実, マニュアル,基準, エビデンス.
Used when you need to emphasize that an action is reasonable/conforms to standards.
If you want to emphasize “following, staying close to a direction/criteria” during the process, consider 「～に沿って」.

～に基づいて expresses “based on, on the grounds of” an objective basis (data, facts, laws, standards, plans) for carrying out an action/making a decision/giving an evaluation.
• Focuses on the foundation/basis underlying the action.
• Often used with verbs such as: 判断する, 決定する, 設計する, 作成する, 評価する, 対応する.
• Different from ～をもとに: 「に基づいて」 emphasizes officialness, objectivity, and standards; 「をもとに」 can carry the nuance of “taking inspiration/material” to adapt or compile.
• Close to ～に則って/に即して (in accordance with norms and standards), but 「に基づいて」 emphasizes the “basis” more than “strict compliance”.
• Can also be used with a negative basis to advise against something: 感情に基づいて判断してはいけない。
fields.notes:
• Memory tip: 「基」= foundation, 「基づく」= based on a foundation.
• If the sentence emphasizes a source of inspiration or reference material → prefer 「～をもとに」.
• The linking form 「N に基づく/に基づいた N」 is very natural in report headings.
• In casual spoken language you may hear 「にもとづいて」 pronounced as plain kana. meaning_vi: Taking ～ as a basis, grounds ⏐ explain: Used in written language. ⏐ examples: 1. この工事は市の計画に基づいて進められます。
This construction work is being carried out based on the city's plan.
2. 長年の経験に基づき新入社員を教育する。
New employees are trained based on many years of experience.
mistakes: Confusing it with ～をもとに: for “a movie based on a novel” → 「小説をもとに」 is more natural than 「に基づいて」.
Using it for “following a route” → use 「～に沿って」 instead of 「～に基づいて」.
Wrong part of speech: what comes before 「に基づいて」 must be a noun.
The JLPT often asks you to choose among 「に基づいて／に沿って／をもとに」 based on context: laws/regulations → 「に基づいて」; routes/criteria → 「に沿って」; creating/compiling → 「をもとに」.

examples: She lived up to her parents' expectations and got a job at a good company.
In response to our customers' requests, we have decided to open 30 minutes earlier.
In response to customer feedback, we will extend our business hours.
They gave a brilliant performance that lived up to the fans' expectations.
We developed a new product that meets market demand.
In response to the request, the Self-Defense Forces were dispatched.
fields.explain:
Positive nuance; often used with verbs expressing concrete actions:実施する,開催する,改善する,延長する,用意する,開発する.
Can be used in both spoken and written language; the form 「に応え」 has a written-language nuance.
The subject acts with volition and effort to respond.
To say “respond to cheers”, you often see:声援に応えて手を振る.

～に応えて expresses the action of “meeting, responding to” expectations, requests, appeals, needs, etc. from other people/society.
• The target is usually a wish/expectation/request from people or organizations: 期待, 要望, 依頼, 要請, リクエスト, 声援, ニーズ, 需要.
• Emphasizes the subject's effort to satisfy them in response.
• Different from ～に応じて: 「に応じて」 = “depending on/in accordance with (conditions)”, while 「に応えて」 = “in response to (a request/expectation)” from another party.
fields.notes:
• Kanji distinction: 応える (meet expectations) vs 答える (answer a question).
• Common phrases in the news: 「市民の要望に応えて～」「需要に応える～」.
• Polite negative in announcements: 「ご期待に応えることができません。」
meaning_vi: 相手(あいて)からの希望(きぼう)、要求(ようきゅう)、等(など)に応(おう)じて
To respond to
examples: 1. 選手たちは会場の声援にこたえて手を振った/大活躍した。
In response to the cheers from the venue, the athletes waved.
2. 学校は学生の用法にこたえ、図書館の利用時間を延長した。
The school extended the library's opening hours in response to the students' wishes.
3. きょうの晩ご飯は、子どもたちのリクエストに応えてハンバーグにした。
For dinner tonight, we had hamburger steak at the children's request.
4. 私は成績が悪く、親の期待に応えることができなかった。
My grades were poor, and I couldn't live up to my parents' expectations. meaning_vi: In response to, responding to… ⏐ explain: Responding to an action from outside. N is a noun indicating questions, expectations, wishes, etc.
Kanji: 応えて・応え・答える ⏐ examples: 1. 客の意見にこたえて、営業時間を延長する。
Extend business hours in response to customers' opinions.
2. 親の期待にこたえ、がんばった。
I worked hard to live up to my parents' expectations.
mistakes: Confusing it with 「に応じて」. If the meaning is “depending on quantity/conditions” → use 「に応じて」, not 「に応えて」.
Using 「質問に応えて」 instead of 「質問に答えて」 → likely to be considered unnatural. Standard: 質問に答えて.
Wrong part of speech: what comes before 「に応えて」 must be a noun.
JLPT collocation trap: 需要/期待/要望/声援 usually go with 「に応えて」; 人数/状況/年齢/収入 usually go with 「に応じて」.

examples: The amount of tax is determined according to income.
We will add more seats depending on the number of people.
We change our countermeasures depending on the situation.
You can choose a class suited to your ability.
We will adjust the departure time depending on the weather.
It can be customized according to the customer's wishes.
fields.explain:
Neutral-to-formal nuance, suitable for announcements, regulations, and service descriptions.
Used with verbs indicating change/adjustment:変わる,変える,決める,調整する,分ける,対応する.
To express “changing together” naturally over time/a process, you can also use 「～につれて／～に従って」.

～に応じて expresses change/adjustment to suit conditions, situations, quantities, degree, ability, etc.
• Often used when the result/measure is flexible according to the input criteria.
• Typical targets: 年齢, 能力, 状況, 希望, 人数, 収入, 需要, レベル, 天候, 予算.
• Different from ～によって (because of/depending on), 「に応じて」 emphasizes corresponding adjustment, not necessarily a cause.
• Different from ～に応えて: 「に応じて」 does not mean “responding to” someone's specific expectations/requests.
fields.notes:
• Memory tip: 「応」 = respond/cope → 「に応じて」 = “respond accordingly”.
• The linking form 「N に応じた N」 is very common in advertising/services: ご希望に応じたプラン.
• When the subject “accepts/responds” (agrees to take part), the verb 「応じる」 is used on its own: 募集に応じる＝apply.
meaning_vi: 変化(へんか)、耐用性(たいようせい)に合(あ)わせて
Depending on, in accordance with
examples: 1. 本校では学生のレベルに応じてクラス分けを行います。
At this school, classes are divided according to the students' level.
2. 学習目的の多様化に応じ、教授法や教材にも工夫が求められる。
In line with the diversification of learning purposes, teaching methods and materials also need to be more carefully devised.
3. 非常時には、状況に応じて柔軟に対処することが必要だ。
In an emergency, you need to deal flexibly with the situation.
4. 最近は電気製品もカラフルになり、好みに応じて色が選べる。
These days, electrical appliances have also become colorful, so you can choose a color according to your taste.
5. 当ホテルでは、お客様一人一人のニーズに応じたサービスを提供いたします。
At our hotel, we offer services that meet the needs of each guest.
6. 他からの働きかけに対してこたえる
7. ボランティアの募集に多くの若者が応じた。
Many young people responded to the call for volunteers.
8. 注文が殺到し、応じきれなくなった。
Orders flooded in, and we could no longer keep up with them.
mistakes: Confusing it with 「に応えて」: if it is “someone's request/expectation” → use 「に応えて」, not 「に応じて」.
Using 「によって」 instead of 「に応じて」 loses the nuance of “flexible adjustment”.
Wrong part of speech: it attaches only to nouns.
JLPT collocation trap: 料金/課題/クラス/対応/調整 → often go with 「に応じて」.

examples: A story like that is bound to be a lie.
If it's your first time, of course you'll be nervous.
That high-end restaurant is bound to be expensive.
He's busy, so he definitely won't be able to come today.
Isn't this problem hard? — No way, of course it's hard.
With an attitude like that, you're bound to be misunderstood.
fields.explain:
Often used in conversation; to be more polite, use 「～に決まっています」.
The colloquial contracted form is 「～に決まってる」, emphasized with 「じゃん／でしょ」.
Can sound pushy; be careful when speaking to superiors.
Can be used with the past to make a conjecture about the past: ～に決まっていた.

～に決まっている expresses a strong subjective judgment: “surely…, of course… (based on the speaker's conjecture/context/experience)”.
• Assertive nuance, sometimes implying criticism/asserting the obvious.
• Used with both affirmative and negative: ～ないに決まっている.
• Different from ～に違いない: 「に決まっている」 is more emotional and colloquial; 「に違いない」 is more formal and objective.
• Not used when the speaker already knows for sure from solid evidence (in that case, simply state the fact).
fields.notes:
1) Easily confused with ～に違いない.
→ ～に決まっている is a very strong assertion, carrying the emotion “of course”.
2) Often used in spoken language, with a subjective nuance.
→ Can easily sound assertive, sometimes a bit pushy.
3) Not used when the degree of certainty is low.
→ If it is only “probably”, use ～だろう／～かもしれない.
mistakes: Mechanically adding だ before に決まっている with N/な: 「学生だに決まっている」 is usually unnatural → 「学生に決まっている」.
Using it for an obvious, already known fact instead of a conjecture → redundant and inappropriate.
Confusing it with 「に違いない」 in formal written language: the JLPT usually chooses 「に違いない」 rather than 「に決まっている」.
The tone is too strong and impolite in business emails; use 「～に違いありません／～と思われます」 instead.

examples: This road runs along the coastline.
Please handle it according to the manual.
Classes proceed according to the curriculum.
We introduced an evaluation system in line with company policy.
A walking path along the river has been built.
We will revise the plan in line with the budget.
fields.explain:
Used to emphasize not deviating from guidelines/criteria/a path.
Common nouns:方針,規則,規定,目標,計画, マニュアル, カリキュラム,地図,境界線,川/道/線.
Suitable for guidelines/procedure documents; in geographical descriptions it has the literal meaning “along”.

～に沿って has two main layers of meaning:
• Along (literal meaning): going/moving along a road, riverbank, route, or boundary.
• Closely following (figurative meaning): carrying out work in line with an established policy, criteria, plan, guideline, or goal, avoiding deviation.
• Emphasizes adherence to a “guiding line/criteria”, unlike 「に基づいて」 (emphasizes an objective basis) and 「に応じて」 (emphasizes flexible adjustment).
fields.notes:
• Visualize it: draw “a line” and then follow along that line → 「に沿って」.
• In quality procedures, a common pair is: マニュアルに沿って（carry out）＋ 記録に基づいて（prove）.
• For places/roads, you can replace it with 「沿い（ぞい）」 as in 名詞＋沿いの道. explain: Expresses doing something according to, following, or conforming to something.
Kanji: 沿い ⏐ examples: 1. 資料に沿って、ご説明いたします。
I will explain following the materials.
2. お客様ひとりひとりのご希望に沿った旅行プランをお作りします。
We create travel plans in line with the wishes of each customer.
mistakes: Confusing it with 「に基づいて」: if you need to emphasize “a scientific/data basis”, prefer 「に基づいて」.
Confusing it with 「に応じて」: 「に沿って」 does not express “changing flexibly depending on conditions”.
Using it with verbs of change over time such as 「増える/減る」 to express proportional change → 「につれて／に従って」 is more natural.
Wrong part of speech: what comes before 「に沿って」 is a noun.

fields.connection: V plain form + に過ぎない に過ぎません / N + (である) / Na + (である) / Aい
examples: That kid is very mature, but is still just a high school student.
He says all sorts of things, but he's merely making excuses.
I've only passed the first-round exam. The hard part starts now.
That's nothing more than a rumor.
His success was merely a matter of good luck.
This graph merely shows a trend.
fields.explain:
Usually placed at the end of a clause to conclude by downplaying: …に過ぎない。
Used in objective/argumentative writing; it avoids the sense of a direct attack more than ただの…だ.
Used with emphasizing words: ただ/単なる/所詮+ N + に過ぎない → strengthens the low evaluation.
Suitable for reports, academic writing, and news; it can also be used in conversation but sounds serious.

• Core meaning: asserts a small, limited degree/substance: “only… nothing more; not exceeding…”.
• Discourse implication: downplays importance, negates exaggeration/expectations.
• With figures: emphasizes that they are for reference only/not absolute (この数字は目安に過ぎない).
• More formal and objective nuance than だけだ; often used in writing, reports, and presentations.
• Not used to express obligation/rules; purely an evaluation of degree.
fields.notes:
• After a long clause, use であるに過ぎない to make the sentence sound formal and emphasize its rationality.
• In debates, it can be combined with たかが/所詮 to lower the value of the target: たかが噂に過ぎない。
• Be careful with the nuance toward the other person: it can easily be taken as belittling their effort/value.
meaning_vi: ただ～たけだ（程度(ていど)の低(ひく)さを強調(きょうちょう)）
Merely
examples: 1. その航空機事故で助かったのは、５００人中４人にすぎなかった。
Only 4 out of 500 people survived that plane crash.
2. 汚職事件が摘発されたが、あんなものは氷山一角にすぎないと思われない。
Although the corruption case was exposed, that is only the tip of the iceberg.
3. 彼女はロシア話ができるといっても、ちょっとした挨拶ができるにすぎない。
She says she can speak Russian, but she can only manage simple greetings.
4. 「お礼だなんて、とんでもない。当然の子をしたにすぎないんですから」
[No need to thank me, I only did what anyone should do]
──────
1. ①　５％以下にすぎない
Only 5% or less
2. ②　高校に進学しない人は、５％以下にすぎない。
People who do not go on to high school account for only 5% or less.
3. ③　彼のスピーチは長かったが、同じことを言っているにすぎなかった。
His speech was long, but he was only saying the same things. explain: Used to emphasize a low degree: “Only to that extent, no more.”
Formal sentence style. ⏐ examples: 1. 単なる言い間違いにすぎない。
It is simply nothing more than a slip of the tongue.
2. 簡単な日常英会話ができるにすぎない。
I can merely hold a simple everyday conversation in English.
mistakes: Confusing it with しかない: しかない = “have no choice but to”, while に過ぎない = “merely”.
Dropping である when formality is needed with Na/N: writing 重要だに過ぎない is unnatural → 重要であるに過ぎない.
Overusing it in casual speech makes the sentence sound distant; replace it with だけだ when you need to sound natural.
Wrong placement: この結果は仮説に過ぎない（correct）; 仮説過ぎない（incorrect).
